name: level1-playthrough-revolt
description: Level 1 worker revolt scenario: an aggressive 16-hole krackle blast, then a 12-strong crew with no rest relief sinks wellBeing to its floor and the site revolts. #1431 (rebuilt after #1313 froze the mine at level end): the opening is funded ($1,050,000, solvent throughout) and two living quarters keep wellBeing up through the drill and the blast, so the blast fires at tick 478 while the level is still running (killing the idle crew near the pattern). wellBeing then falls to 0 and stays there for REVOLT_TICKS, and the worker revolt (levelEndReason 'worker_revolt', never bankruptcy) is the only end, at tick 619. Everything after it asserts the frozen state.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1) through #5 driver, plus vehicles #1 drill_rig through #4 rock_fragmenter (all unmanned). Cost is free -- does not change starting cash. The file's own 7 hand-hired employees below become #6-#12.

#1379: the default site policy (shift_8h, threshold 60) is always in force, so a staffed crew is force-rested and cared for by default. This file is about the revolt that neglect causes, so neglect is now explicit: continuous mode with the lowest rest threshold (0) never forces rest, leaving wellBeing to drain exactly as the pre-#1379 no-policy baseline did.

#553: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) is still a mesh nobody can drive until employee #1, the only qualified driller on the roster at this point, boards it. #921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.

#553 sandbox-measured finding: staffed:true parks its 4 vehicles in a row at (0,2)/(2,2)/(4,2)/(6,2), and on dusty_hollow's terrain that row sits inside the map's only ramp corridor out of the spawn corner -- tickVehicleOnNavGrid recomputes the same A* path every tick (avoidVehicles:false) and only refuses the immediate next cell if another vehicle already occupies it (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle), so the drill_rig (vehicle #1) advances exactly one cell to (1,2) and then waits forever behind the unmanned debris_hauler parked at (2,2) -- confirmed by direct trace: 40+ ticks stuck at (1,2), waitingTicks climbing, holeCount never leaving 0. This file never uses a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter (zero hauling/fragment-breaking anywhere in its script), so scrapping the blocker -- and the other two idle vehicles that would otherwise just draw maintenance upkeep for nothing -- clears the corridor and turns dead weight into cash. #929: opens the Fleet panel itself. The step that used to open it with a real toolbar click became a bootstrap command under #921, and UIManager only updates a visible panel -- a Fleet panel nobody opened renders no vehicle cards at all, so this click had nothing to land on.
rock_digger #3 was never in the drill_rig's path, but this file has no use for it either -- scrapped for the same reason as #2: pure upkeep with nothing to show for it.

rock_fragmenter #4, same reasoning. Sandbox-measured residual proceeds across all three scraps ($10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800) fund the 7 hires below without touching the $50,000 opening balance.
#553: this and the following 6 hires are the file's own original crew, renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5 first.

#553: employee #7. Deliberately left unlicensed for driving.drill_rig -- sandbox-measured, licensing this driller as a backup only adds a second casualty to blast 1 (they end up standing near the pattern too) without changing the outcome, since patterns 2-4 stall on the missing vehicle regardless of how many licensed drillers are left alive (see the note on the pattern-2 drill_plan step below).

#1431: living quarters keep wellBeing above zero through the drill and blast, so the revolt lands after the blast instead of before it.

Wait for the crew to finish the living quarters before the drilling begins.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:6,5
steps.description: #1151: shifted one cell east. Under the 30-degree slope gate (5,11) sits outside the crew's climb-reachable patch on dusty_hollow, so no driller could ever claim that hole and the pattern stalled at 15 of 16 forever. Measured by replaying this file's own steps to this point; start:6,5 is the nearest origin whose whole 4x4 grid is reachable.
Advance until the first event interrupts (or 283 ticks pass); the crew is still drilling and wellBeing is held up by the living quarters.

#596/#597-followup: this event is now union_unlucky_days, not weather_minor_tremor -- #596's event-pool dedup fix changed the RNG draw order for which event becomes eligible first. Option 0 ("Lucky Charms") is a fixed, RNG-free delta sandbox-traced to cashDelta:-2000, scoreDelta.wellBeing:+5 -- no safety effect, unlike the old weather_minor_tremor draw. tickCount dropped from this step's own expect: it doesn't move during an event-choose (no ticking happens here), and the tick-283 step above already covers it directionally.
Wait for the crew to sink all 16 holes (the pattern drills in the field, not instantly).
Charges all drilled holes with 8 kg krackle -- the aggressive blast this scenario is named for.
Drain the charge orders at speed 8 (charging is real work); the level is still running here.
Auto-sequence the charged holes.
Fires the 16-hole krackle pattern while the level is still running: the blast comes first, the revolt after.

Advance (at speed 8) until the level ends. wellBeing has sunk to 0 and stays there for REVOLT_TICKS (120) consecutive ticks: the worker revolt is the only end, and it lands after the blast. The mine freezes at that tick (#1313). Cash stays far above the bankruptcy threshold throughout.
#1313: the mine is frozen after the revolt -- a tick advances neither cash nor the clock.
